title: Admission contract and runtime-compatibility notes for third-party model entries
creator: Priya Shah
description: Clarify the admission contract for community/third-party model submissions to the catalog and define the normative runtime-compatibility and pinning behaviour that the serving layer and Console will expose to customers. This PRD focuses on explicit, machine-readable compatibility signals, a deterministic pin/fallback policy, required telemetry and evaluation checks for admission, and the acceptance criteria necessary for Safe Launch in the hosted catalog and Dedicated/Private product tiers.
scope: In scope: define admission checklist for new community model entries (execution test-suite, inference electrical/latency profile, tokenization parity check), required compatibility metadata fields, default pinning semantics and documented fallback ordering, minimal telemetry events for model regressions, and Console UI copy for pin/fallback state.

In scope: runtime contract for pin enforcement (how long to respect soft pins vs hard pins), automated rollback triggers based on quality or latency regressions, and guidance for Dedicated/Private differences (customer override options).
Out of scope: changes to model training, upstream model provenance verification beyond declared provenance fields, or a fully automated security-sandboxing system (this is a follow-on workstream).
Out of scope: marketplace/legal onboarding and commercial licensing flow—this ticket only defines the catalog admission and runtime compatibility contract required by product and runtime teams.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Admission checklist documented and published as a machine-readable schema (JSON schema) with at least these fields: model_architecture, tokenizer_hash, longest_supported_seq, fp/quantization_profiles, provenanced_weights_url, test-inference-hash. Schema must be PR-reviewed and merged to repository.

AC-2: Runtime-compatibility matrix defined that maps model variants to supported kernel profiles and minimum hardware class (e.g., A100-40GB, H100-80GB, CPU-fallback). Matrix must include deterministic fallback order for at least 3 common mismatch scenarios.

AC-3: Pinning policy documented: soft-pin semantics (duration 14 days by default, can be overridden by customer for Dedicated/Private), hard-pin semantics (explicit vendor-signed pin that requires manual override). Runtime must honor pin precedence and log pin_state changes via telemetry.

AC-4: Evaluation checks automated: a lightweight inference acceptance suite (sample prompt set with expected metrics) runs on new community entries and the results are attached to the catalog entry page. Failures block admission until triaged.
AC-5: Console UI mockups for catalog entry pin state and compatibility notes are produced and design-approved; copy includes guidance on fallback behavior and customer override affordances.

AC-6: Telemetry events defined and instrumented: model_regression_alert, pin_state_change, fallback_triggered, admission_evaluation_result. Events must include model_key, variant, runtime_profile, and a reason code.

AC-7: A minimal rollout plan and rollback playbook exists; on-call runbook references exact telemetry thresholds for automated fallback and manual rollback steps. Playbook is accessible from the catalog entry page.
decisions: D1: Use a JSON schema that lives in the model-catalog repo as the canonical admission contract; downstream services should read from this single source of truth.
D2: Default soft-pin window set to 14 days to allow fast updates while giving customers deterministic behavior; Dedicated/Private customers can request longer windows via support tickets.
D3: Telemetry will be event-based with structured reason codes rather than free-text to enable automated alerting and runbook hooks.

D4: The runtime will attempt up to two automatic fallbacks in order of decreasing cost/perf (exact order: same-variant-quantized -> compatible-architecture-variant -> last-resort CPU) before returning a user-facing degraded response. This order is subject to capacity and SLA constraints.
tradeoffs: T1: Strict admission checks improve reliability but increase onboarding friction for small community contributors. Mitigation: provide a lightweight permissive channel for experimental models that opt-out of catalog visibility (experimental flag).
T2: Longer default pins reduce change churn for customers but slow security/bug fixes rollout. Mitigation: allow emergency hard-unpin mechanism for security-critical fixes with audit trail.
T3: Adding more telemetry increases storage and retention cost. Mitigation: sample low-volume events and keep retention short by default, with opt-in extended retention for paid tiers.

open_questions: Q1: What is the minimal acceptance suite size (n prompts) that balances signal vs cost for admission evaluation? Suggested range 10-50 — need runtime opinion.
Q2: For Dedicated customers, should we expose pin duration as a self-service control in Console or keep it support-mediated?
Q3: Are there legal constraints about storing provenanced_weights_url for certain community-supplied weights? (Legal to advise.)
Q4: What sampling rate for fallback_triggered telemetry is acceptable for large customers to keep costs manageable?
Q5: Should experimental models be visible to internal users by default (for QA) or remain hidden until explicitly published?
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): Publish JSON schema and admission checklist; enable experimental flag for internal-only model visibility. Run manual onboarding on 3 representative community models.
Phase 2 (beta): Open admission to a small external cohort; monitor telemetry events for fallback and regression alerts for 14 days. Collect customer feedback and iterate on pin defaults.

Phase 3 (GA): Flip catalog visibility on for broader public intake, enforce admission checks by default, and document runbook steps for automated fallback/rollback. Announce to customers via release notes.

Rollback plan: If widespread regressions occur post-admission, use telemetry to identify offending model_keys and either soft-unpublish or hard-unpin per playbook. Ensure manual rollback instructions available to SRE and Support.
